cases.title: AI Research Scientist - Datadog AI Research (DAIR)
locations: New York, New York, USA; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA
cases.text: As a Research Scientist on our team, you will partner with Research Engineers, working on fundamental research problems and collaborating with Datadog's product and engineering teams to translate research advances into products. Building on our track record of AI-powered solutions (e.g., Bits AI , Bits Evolve , and our time series foundation model ), Datadog AI Research tackles high-risk, high-reward problems grounded in real-world challenges in cloud observability and security. We are focused on two research areas: World Models for Observability -- Training multimodal foundation models that learn the joint dynamics of distributed systems across metrics, traces, logs, topology, and events. These models power advanced forecasting, anomaly detection, root cause analysis, counterfactual simulation ("what if?"), and provide a learned planning backbone for our autonomous agents. Trained Agents for Observability -- Post-training models to operate autonomously across Datadog's domain. SRE incident response is our first target, with a clear path to code repair, security response, and infrastructure optimization. We build the simulation environments, RL training loops, and evaluation infrastructure needed to train agents that match or surpass frontier models at a fraction of the cost. What You'll Do: Conduct research in generative AI and machine learning, building specialized foundation models and trained agents for observability Train multimodal models on large-scale, diverse telemetry data (metrics, logs, traces, topology, events) using distributed training infrastructure Design and build simulated environments and RL training loops for on-policy agent training and evaluation Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Product, Engineering) to integrate capabilities like multimodal world modeling and autonomous agents into Datadog's products Stay at the forefront of foundation models, world models, and RL-based agent research Contribute to research publications, present at top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML), and help open-source key model artifacts and benchmarks Who You Are: You hold a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, with deep expertise in areas like generative modeling, world models, AI agents, reinforcement learning, or multimodal learning (or have equivalent experience) You have extensive experience designing and implementing deep learning models and agents, with a strong background in distributed training frameworks (e.g., DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM) and ML libraries (PyTorch) You have a track record of impactful publications at top-tier venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, TMLR) You are familiar with efficient training, post-training, and inference techniques for large foundation models You can explain complex models and research findings to both technical and non-technical audiences Bonus Points (any of the following): Experience bridging research and real-world product applications, especially with large foundation models, world models, or RL-trained agents Passion for pushing the boundaries of AI with a focus on customer impact and scalable deployment Experience writing production data pipelines and applications Hands-on experience with GPU programming and optimization, including CUDA Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply. Benefits and Growth: Competitive global benefits New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) Opportunity to collaborate closely with colleagues across the Datadog offices in New York City and Paris Opportunity to attend and present at conferences and meetups Intra-departmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking An inclusive company culture, ability to join our Community Guilds (Datadog employee resource groups) Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog. About Datadog: Datadog (NASDAQ: DDOG) is a global SaaS business, delivering a rare combination of growth and profitability. We are on a mission to break down silos and solve complexity in the cloud age by enabling digital transformation, cloud migration, and infrastructure monitoring of our customers’ entire technology stacks. Built by engineers, for engineers, Datadog is used by organizations of all sizes across a wide range of industries. Together, we champion professional development, diversity of thought, innovation, and work excellence to empower continuous growth. Join the pack and become part of a collaborative, pragmatic, and thoughtful people-first community where we solve tough problems, take smart risks, and celebrate one another. cases.title: Corporate Communications Senior Manager, Executive Communications Programs
cases.text: As a Corporate Communication Senior Manager focused on Executive Communications Programs, you will build and scale Datadog's integrated thought leadership program — spanning executive communications, earned and owned channels, and events — with a focus on extending it across priority regions. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution: you'll translate leadership priorities into playbooks, frameworks, and measurable programs, then run them day to day. Success hinges on connecting dots across initiatives and partner teams to find new opportunities to tell Datadog's story through our executive voices. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. What You'll Do: Partner with the Global Head of Corporate Comms to develop and execute an integrated thought leadership program with clear objectives and measurable outcomes. Build the operating framework behind the program — playbooks, cross-team coordination models, and repeatable processes that let it scale across regions. Identify opportunities to put Datadog thought leaders in front of the right audiences, including vetting speaking engagements: where we need to be, what we should be saying, and which channel (social, traditional media, stage) delivers the most impact. Work with US Comms and Social leads to augment existing campaigns and build evergreen thought leadership programs across channels. Partner with Field Marketing on event strategy and execution, with a focus on advancing our key narratives around AI and security. Develop strategic messaging for senior executives across key business moments — corporate announcements, company milestones, and other high-priority communications. Serve as the Corporate Comms "captain": keep a bird's-eye view of initiatives across the company, manage day-to-day coordination with partner teams, and flag where Datadog leaders can advance our goals. You are an exceptional writer and storyteller, with experience ghostwriting executive communications, speeches, bylines, blogs, etc.. cases.title: Curriculum Manager
cases.text: Reporting to the Senior Manager, Enablement Curriculum and working across a cross-functional Enablement team, you'll build learning experiences that hold up in the field - objectives, practice, assessment, and the content that carries them. This is a builder's role. You'll decide how the learning actually works, and you'll own the quality of what ships. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. Who you are: An owner: You take pride in your outputs and their outcomes. You take ownership from design through launch and everything that comes after it. An innovator: You challenge the status quo, bring new ideas, and look for ways to improve what already exists. An agile problem solver: You shift seamlessly between detail and big picture to meet the moment, adapting to change with a solutions-oriented mindset. A lifelong learner: You challenge assumptions and use curiosity to drive continuous improvement. A trusted advisor: You ask sharp questions, synthesize complex ideas, and build relationships to understand and explain ambiguous concepts. A clear communicator: You bring structure, clarity and polish to your work - written, verbal or visual. What you’ll do: Build the curriculum for Global Commercial Customer Success. Develop high-quality enablement content (instructor-led materials, facilitator guides, eLearning, job aids and assessments) for both individual contributors and their frontline leaders, built to instructional design and adult learning principles. Build within the learner journey. Contribute to and build the components of role-specific journeys (onboarding, everboarding and on-demand) inside the curriculum arc for your area. Know what good looks like. Translate performance expectations into observable behaviors and clear proficiency standards. Turn business problems into learning design. Partner with Program Management and Strategy & Operations to identify the key behaviors and knowledge a program needs to shift, and design the learning that gets there. Own the learning objectives for the programs you build, and design assessments that measure against them. Build programs that drive durable behavior change. Design practice, reinforcement and refresher paths into programs. Develop content with build partners and other Enablement teams, including subject matter experts who don't report to you, and manage your build schedule so programs meet quality standards and timelines. Partner with facilitators, operations teams and test audiences to ensure successful rollouts of new and updated programs. Help maintain the programs you build, keeping content accurate, current and consistent after launch. Use AI well. Use AI for scripting, storyboards, assessment drafting and learner-feedback analysis, and coach peers on responsible AI-assisted content creation. Your experience: 4–5 years in Enablement, Learning & Development, Sales, Revenue Operations or similar (bonus points for a combination) Proven track record designing and building enablement content with measurable learner impact Working knowledge of adult learning principles and a learning design methodology (e.g. ADDIE or equivalent) Ability to design clean, intuitive learning materials across modalities — instructor-led, eLearning, simulation, job aids — blending instructional and visual design Ability to manage multi-week content projects independently and deliver quality on short timeframes Experience partnering with subject matter experts and stakeholders in a go-to-market organization Comfort using learner data — completion, assessment and feedback — to find gaps and improve programs Understanding of sales processes and challenges in a high-velocity environment Familiarity with at least one sales methodology (e.g. Command of the Message, MEDDICC, Sandler, Challenger, value-based selling) or equivalent Bonus Points: Experience in Sales, Sales Development, Sales Leadership or Sales Operations Formal grounding in instructional design and adult learning (e.g. ATD CPTD, CPLP or equivalent) Experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS or technology company Experience with an LMS and content authoring tools Experience building content that other people facilitate Basic understanding of the observability, DevOps or cloud space Datadog values people from all walks of life. cases.title: Senior Security Engineer, Vulnerability Management
locations: Boston, Massachusetts, USA; New York, New York, USA
cases.text: Senior Security Engineer, Vulnerability Management Here at Datadog, we think about vulnerability management a little differently. We embrace open source software, recognize our role in the software supply chain, and see attackers weaponizing vulnerabilities faster than ever. We are looking for a Senior Security Engineer who can combine vulnerability-management judgment with hands-on engineering to help us scale and improve our vulnerability lifecycle across Datadog’s multi-cloud products and services. In this role, you will turn ambiguous security problems into clear solutions, and work with engineering teams to address root causes and develop technical controls that reduce vulnerabilities earlier in the SDLC. You’ll use AI and automation to help scale the overall vulnerability lifecycle across Datadog. You will use data and sound technical judgment to prioritize risk, and partner with security, product, platform, and compliance teams to bring scalable solutions into practice. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. What You’ll Do Work across the vulnerability lifecycle from detection and impact assessment through risk-based prioritization, remediation, and verification. Use AI and automation to build tools, services, and workflows that make security ideas concrete, validate them quickly, and create alignment for scalable implementation. Reduce engineering toil through a “PRs, not tickets” approach, using automation to enrich findings, identify ownership, recommend or deliver fixes, and track outcomes. Analyze recurring vulnerabilities and remediation failures to identify root causes and opportunities to prevent issues earlier in the SDLC. Partner with SDLC Security, Product Security, platform teams, and engineering teams to balance technical constraints, business impact, and risk; communicate concerns early and pair problems with actionable options. Provide evidence and subject matter expertise for vulnerability management processes and controls for multiple compliance frameworks (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI, FedRAMP, ISO) Who You Are You have experience identifying, prioritizing, and driving remediation of vulnerabilities in large software, cloud, or infrastructure environments. You can independently solve complex technical problems using one or more programming languages such as Go, Python, or Java. You have experience with cloud-native or multi-cloud environments, containers or orchestration platforms, infrastructure as code, and modern software-delivery workflows. You have experience reproducing and validating externally reported vulnerabilities. You use data, exploitability, exposure, technical context, and business impact to make and explain risk decisions. You are comfortable making progress without a complete specification: you break problems down, test assumptions, fail fast, document tradeoffs, and adjust when new information emerges. You use AI-assisted tools thoughtfully, validate their output, and can explain the reasoning behind your decisions. You influence across security, engineering, product, and compliance teams through clear communication, technical credibility, and solutions that reduce friction. You have a BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related scientific field, or equivalent practical experience Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply.
